prediction.raw: I would say 0, which means "NTA" (Not The Asshole) in this scenario. The person who drove the wrong way up to the ATM was in the wrong, as they disregarded the clearly marked arrows and the logical setup of the drive-up ATM. By doing so, they put themselves and others at risk of an accident. You, on the other hand, were following the rules and waiting your turn. When the other driver asked you to move, you didn't have to oblige, especially since you were already running late for class and there was no one behind you. It's understandable that you felt annoyed and frustrated by the situation, and it's reasonable that you didn't want to reward the other driver's reckless behavior by backing up. By not moving, you were standing up for yourself and asserting your right to use the ATM in a safe and orderly manner. Your friend's suggestion that you should have backed up because there was no one behind you doesn't take into account the fact that the other driver was in the wrong and that you had a right to be there. It's not about being a "dick" or not; it's about standing up for yourself and following the rules.
